change: Switched on browser sign-in and personal client keys, which already shipped in release 8 and were switched off by host configuration.
meaning: A person the operator has invited can sign in with the identity provider, receive a server-owned account, and create and revoke personal client keys. The public sign-up form stays closed until the account email work lands.
how_it_was_applied: The proposed blocks were validated offline with the real configuration classes, together with four known-wrong variants that must be refused: a sign-up form without account admission, automatic administration authority, an insecure identity origin, and a customer key policy that grants administration.
The existing host configuration was copied to /data/host.json.backup-before-signin on the volume.
The new configuration was written beside it and loaded with the real loader inside the running machine before anything was replaced.
Only then was it moved into place.
The identity publishable key was staged as a deployment secret with tools/stage_service_secrets.py, so its value never appeared in a command line, a log or a report.
The same image digest was redeployed to apply the staged secret and restart the machine. No source changed and no image was built.
rollback: Move /data/host.json.backup-before-signin back into place and redeploy the same image digest. The staged key can stay; it is read only when the browser identity block is present.
known_limits: No person has signed in through this path yet.
The public sign-up form is closed. Accounts are created by invitation until the account email work lands.
The confirmation redirect still names the platform hostname because the public base address is unchanged. Moving it to the branded hostname is planned with the account email release.
The catalogue still holds one diagnostic item, so a new account sees very little until the approved catalogue is published.
